pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: Urine oxidizing to a dark port-wine color on light exposure, combined with the classic pentad of severe neurovisceral abdominal pain out of proportion to exam, autonomic instability, hyponatremia (SIADH), and ascending motor neuropathy triggered by fasting and sulfonamides. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: A metabolic defect due to a deficiency in porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD) in the heme synthesis pathway. Caloric deprivation and CYP450-inducing xenobiotics (e.g., sulfonamides) trigger the hepatic enzyme ALAS1, causing a massive, catastrophic accumulation of the neurotoxic heme precursors delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG), precipitating central, autonomic, and peripheral nervous system breakdown.
